scenario: A charter-industry database records only voyages exceeding 12 days (the minimum commercial reporting threshold). The observed mean charter duration among recorded voyages is 18.0 days (σ=4.0 days). The true mean over all charters is sought.

data.description: Observed statistics among units exceeding reporting threshold

values.n_observed: only values above threshold are recorded

question: (a) Assuming the true distribution of charter duration is normal with σ=4.0 days, solve for the true population mean μ such that E[X|X>12.0]=18.0. (b) What fraction of all events lie above the above 12-day reporting minimum threshold? (c) By how much does the observed mean overstate the true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: Solving the truncated-normal equation μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 18.0 numerically gives μ≈17.25708. Only 90.6% of all events are actually observed; the observed mean overstates the true mean by ≈0.7429 days.

naive_answer: The true mean charter duration is approximately 18.0 days because that is what the data directly show.
naive_trap: The observed mean is a truncated-normal conditional expectation, not the population mean; it always exceeds the true mean for above-threshold samples.
reasoning_trace: (1) Let α=(t−μ)/σ. (2) E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 18.0 and solve numerically for μ using brentq. (4) Solution: μ≈17.25708. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((12.0−17.25708)/σ)≈0.90562.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 18.0,4.0,12.0
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-17.25708)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.90562)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
